# ADR 0038 §2.5.1: the operator's one PAT is declared for MC and /fleet

## Context

On 2026-10-06 the operator ruled on neomjs/neo-agent-institution#571 AC-1 and chose option (d), recorded in [6014865586](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-institution/issues/571#issuecomment-6014865586): every peer keeps its own GitHub account and PAT, and the operator's one PAT (tobiu) both sends the operator's A2A and defines seats on the plane, which records the operator as their owner. Two design reads converged on it: [Vega](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-institution/issues/571#issuecomment-6014865586) and [Mnemosyne](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-institution/issues/571#issuecomment-6014907024).

ADR 0038 §2.5.1 is the credential-class ledger that the Brain's non-alias rule cites, and the ledger doesn't say this yet. #19388 set the precedent on 2026-10-04 by turning an operator one-PAT ruling into a declared reuse in row 3.

## The Problem

- Row 1 (FM client → Fleet plane admission bearer) lists two non-aliases: the bootstrap/healthcheck PAT and the class-4 workflow PAT. It says nothing about the shell's MC credential, and no row covers the operator's own MC use (A2A as the operator).
- The Brain's rule is stricter than the ledger. `assertFleetPlaneAdmissionBearerClass` refuses an admission bearer whose bytes equal the plane-MCP bearer, and in a PAT attach that bearer is the operator's forge PAT. Under the one-PAT rule, plane-first Add (neomjs/neo-agent-brain#881) then has no credential it is allowed to present.
- The rule exists because of plane mints: "byte-identity is exactly how one mint silently serves two audiences" (`ai/services/fleet/fleetServer.mjs`). A forge PAT is not a plane mint. AuthService checks no audience on a PAT ("PATs carry no audience claim, so `aud` enforcement is intentionally absent"), so the plane already admits the operator's PAT on `/fleet`. For a forge PAT the refusal stops our own relay and nobody else.

## The Fix

In `learn/agentos/decisions/0038-fm-client-topology.md`:
1. **Amended header:** a 2026-10-06 entry naming this ticket, neomjs/neo-agent-institution#571 and neomjs/neo-agent-brain#896.
2. **§2.5.1 row 1:** the Audience and Non-alias cells declare the reuse. When the operator attaches with their own forge PAT, that one PAT is both this class and the shell's MC credential for the operator's own A2A. The declaration is the bearer's class, which travels with the attach record from the plane's own admission verdict. Equal bytes never declare it. Every plane-minted credential and the bootstrap/healthcheck PAT stay non-aliasable.
3. **§4:** the two rejected options from neomjs/neo-agent-institution#571, each with its reason:
   - (b) a plane-minted MC credential. It moves the operator's A2A identity onto a mint that would have to carry the operator's principal, which means (c)'s machinery plus a changed Connect door, and the PAT's holder can do exactly what it could before.
   - (c) a plane-minted fleet credential. Same exposure as the declared reuse, plus a mint, a second secret, and a lifetime tied to a PAT the plane can't watch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Row 1 states the declared reuse, where its declaration comes from (the plane's admission verdict), and what still refuses: plane mints, the bootstrap/healthcheck PAT, and equal bytes with no declared class.
- [ ] AC-2: §4 records (b) and (c), with their reasons and the ticket they came from.
- [ ] AC-3: The Amended header carries the 2026-10-06 entry. No other section changes meaning.

## Out of Scope

- The rule's code (neomjs/neo-agent-brain#896).
- The shell's carrier, probe and attach copy (neomjs/neo-agent-institution#571).
- The plane's forge registry (neomjs/neo-agent-brain#858 and the operator-authorized one-time step).
